title: Blending Context-Dependent Validation Rules via Conditional Flags
pattern: A single entity or validator bundles validation rules for multiple distinct application contexts, using control flags to determine which validation pathways to execute.
why_bad: High accidental complexity. It makes the entity fragile and hard to maintain as new application boundaries emerge. Changing validation behavior in one context risks breaking validations in another.
detection: Validation functions accepting boolean or enum "mode" selectors that guard conditional blocks.
counterexample: General-purpose sanitization (e.g., stripping null bytes) that always runs regardless of context. Marked `Context-dependent`.
source: Andrew Hunt, David Thomas, *The Pragmatic Programmer* (2019), Topic 30, "Transforming Programming", p. 580.
